headline: Third AAP MLA resigns in two days as Kunwar Vijay Pratap quits
content: Chandigarh, Nov 2: In a major development in Punjab's ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Amritsar North MLA, Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, resigned on Monday, following in the footsteps of two other MLAs who resigned the previous day.Singh, a former IPS officer, also sent his resignation letter to the Punjab Assembly Speaker on Monday.He was suspended by the AAP for five years in June 2025 for alleged anti-party activities as he had opposed the arrest of Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader Bikram Singh Majithia in a Disproportionate Assets case.Sharing the information on X, Singh said that he will remain "indebted to you until my last breath for the love and respect you have shown me", referring to the people of the state."With your cooperation and the blessings of the Almighty, we must all unite in a collective effort to rise above the politics of lanes and ribbon-cutting, and transform Punjab—trapped by drugs, extortion, gangsterism, and corruption—back into a progressive and beloved state," he said.Singh asserted that he had achieved "90 per cent targets", adding that his "greatest achievement" is "ending the 'mai-baap' culture in politics and working by considering the public as my source of inspiration"."In the Punjab Legislative Assembly, I always raised the voice of Amritsaris and boldly addressed issues from water and sewage to Circuit House, Company Bagh, dirty drains, Guru Nanak Dev University, Government Medical College, Saroop Rani College, and the Bargari sacrilege case. This was the first time that area-specific issues were raised by me in the Punjab Legislative Assembly by naming lanes and neighbourhoods," he said."Working together with you to formulate a forward strategy, my aim will be to ensure clean politics and transparent administration. My sole purpose is 'Punjab First'. Apart from this, I will have no personal interests," he added.Earlier on Sunday, Singh had hit out at AAP National Convener Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, asserting that the party had strayed from its founding ideals.Pratap's exit follows the resignations of fellow MLAs, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra, who resigned from the AAP's primary membership and the Assembly on Sunday.Pathanmajra, who represents the Sanour Assembly constituency in Patiala district, sent his resignation letter to Arvind Kejriwal, announcing his decision to quit the party with immediate effect.Pathanmajra has been at the centre of several controversies in the past. A rape case was registered against him, following which he travelled to Australia. He was subsequently arrested by the police after returning to India to join the investigation into the case.Meanwhile, Jouramajra, who represents the Samana Assembly constituency and has also served as a minister in the Punjab government, announced his resignation through a social media post.According to media reports, tensions had reportedly been building between him and the party leadership after the AAP high command appointed former senior Shiromani Akali Dal leader Surjit Singh Rakhra as the in-charge of the Samana Assembly constituency.The decision had reportedly left Jouramajra unhappy with the party leadership, as the appointment of another leader as constituency in-charge in his own Assembly seat was viewed as a setback to his political standing and influence in the area.The resignations come at a crucial time for the AAP, which is facing a political challenge ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. --IANS

headline: Fire truck bursts into flames following accident in Udaipur; 2 burnt to death
content: Two men were burnt to death, and two others sustained injuries after a fire tender collided with a trailer before hitting another vehicle and bursting into flames in Rajasthan’s Udaipur district, police said on Sunday.The accident occurred when the fire tender, belonging to a private firm, was travelling from Gujarat towards Udaipur.Rishabhdev Station House Officer Hemant Ahari said the vehicle first rammed into a trailer moving ahead of it and went out of control, before hitting a truck in another lane.The impact caused the fire tender’s cabin to catch fire, trapping three people inside.Locals managed to pull the driver out of the burning vehicle, but the two other occupants were burnt to death. Their identities are yet to be established, police said.The drivers of the fire tender and the trailer have sustained injuries and are undergoing treatment at MB Hospital in Udaipur.Police said efforts are under way to identify the deceased and contact the company that owned the fire truck.

headline: Tens of thousands protest against Narendra Modi regime in Delhi | India
content: Led by Congress party, India’s opposition alliance channels anger over removal of 130 million names from voter roll Thousands of opposition supporters have gathered in Delhi as protests against the Narendra Modi government continue to gather momentum. Led by the Congress party, India’s opposition alliance has brought together supporters from across the country, amid growing anger over a large-scale revision of the country’s voter roll that has seen 130 million names erased. Opposition leaders have alleged the process gives Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata party (BJP) an electoral advantage, and have called for the resignation and impeachment of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. The BJP has denied the claims. Addressing tens of thousands of party workers and supporters, the opposition leader Rahul Gandhi said Kumar had “carried out the biggest crime. He has tried to silence the voice of people, strangulate our country.” Gandhi said the opposition, united under the acronym India (Indian National Developmental Inclusive Alliance), would not let “democracy be finished in the country” and warned Modi: “You can’t run anywhere.”

headline: West Bengal government notifies jobs for kin of those killed in political violence
content: Kolkata The West Bengal government on Sunday (November 1, 2026) issued a notification providing jobs for family members of those killed in political violence, a day after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced the decision on Saturday (October 31, 2026) while addressing a gathering in Paschim Medinipur’s Garbeta. https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/west-bengal/ “Apply to the DM (District Magistrate). We will give Group D jobs to you,” Mr. Adhikari had said, referring to the families that have been at the receiving end of political violence. The notification, signed by West Bengal Chief Secretary Manoj Agarwal on Sunday, stated that one member of the family of each person who had lost their life in political clashes would be provided employment by the State government. West Bengal CM promises CAA certificates to 2.5 lakh Matuas by end of 2026 West Bengal CM promises CAA certificates to 2.5 lakh Matuas by end of 2026 During his first visit to Thakurbari in North 24 Parganas after taking up the office of Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari says West Bengal would have turned into Bangladesh had the BJP not come to power in 2026 West Bengal CM promises CAA certificates to 2.5 lakh Matuas by end of 2026 storyline 1 The appointments will be made at the Group D level as a one-time exception, without affecting normal recruitment. The notification provides a cut-off date from 2001 onwards. Families with victims of political violence over the past 25 years can apply for government jobs. The 25 years marks the approximately 11 years during which the Left Front government was in power in the State, with the remaining years when the Trinamool Congress was in power. West Bengal has recorded several instances of political violence, particularly in the panchayat elections held in the State, over the past few decades. The BJP leadership has alleged that their supporters were targeted by Trinamool Congress after 2016, and that a large number of the party’s supporters were targeted after the 2021 Assembly election. The scheme has several eligibility criteria, which includes that the family’s monthly income should not be more than ₹50,000. The applicant will have to provide details of the incident, along with the FIR, death certificate and relationship with the deceased. A screening committee led by District Magistrates and Superintendents of Police will examine the applications. Vedanta chief meets Suvendu, explores investments in West Bengal Vedanta chief meets Suvendu, explores investments in West Bengal Anil Agarwal says he will leave no stone unturned to invest in Bengal if the right opportunity presents itself; CM says the industrialist made a specific proposal to set up a unit in Asansol Vedanta chief meets Suvendu, explores investments in West Bengal storyline 1 According to the notification, the benefit would be available to one dependent family member of each victim. Eligible applicants will include the spouse, son, daughter or third-gender child of the deceased. In cases where an unmarried person was killed, a brother or sister may also be considered, subject to specified conditions. Only one member from each eligible family will be considered for appointment.

headline: Chandigarh will be country's first drug-free city: Amit Shah lauds city police
content: Chandigarh: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday said Chandigarh will be the first city in the country to become drug-free even as he lauded Chandigarh Police, saying it performed duties in an exemplary manner and set a benchmark across the country..Since 1966, Chandigarh Police has worked tirelessly to safeguard the city, effectively writing a golden chapter in the history of policing across the nation, he said.."I believe that over these 60 years, Chandigarh -- as the heart of the northern region -- has made a successful effort to contribute to the security of all of India," he said while addressing a gathering on the occasion of the 60th Raising Day event of Chandigarh Police..Chandigarh achieves 99.93% literacy rate, becomes fully literate Union Territory.Presenting the President's Colour to the Chandigarh Police, Shah said it is a recognition of the force's six decades of service and dedication..Over the past 60 years, the Chandigarh Police has successfully worked towards safeguarding the entire country, serving as a vital force in the heart of the northern region, he said..Lauding the force, Shah said that with a strength of around 6,000 personnel, various wings, including the Crime Wing, Operation Cell, Security Wing, Traffic Police and PCR, have performed their duties in an exemplary manner and set benchmarks across the country.."Now that we have resolved to build a drug-free India, Chandigarh will be the first city in the country to become drug-free," he said..When the period of terrorism began, Chandigarh too was not left untouched by its impact. During those difficult times, Chandigarh Police demonstrated extraordinary valour and courage, the Union home minister said..Through its dedicated service and good governance, it not only worked to protect Chandigarh but also the rest of India from terrorism, he said..Shah said the three new criminal laws were introduced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Chandigarh, marking the country's transition away from the three punitive laws enacted by the British..Referring to the new criminal laws, he said a total of 8,206 FIRs have been registered from August 4, 2024, until today. "Out of these, Chandigarh Police filed online chargesheets in 7,590 cases, which is a national record.".Hailed as a modern-day 'Chanakya', BJP's Amit Shah is now India's longest serving Union Home Minister.With an increase in the conviction rate, Chandigarh Police managed to secure punishments in 85 per cent of cases, he said.."I believe this serves as an ideal for the country and all its police units that if we implement the new judicial codes effectively, we can ensure punishment for 85 per cent of criminals. Chandigarh has proven this by doing it," he noted..He further said that because of the old laws, police services were defamed by the 'jumla' - 'tareekh pe tareekh', adding that for many years, and sometimes for generations, justice was not served.."Today, I want to tell you that the 85 per cent conviction rate achieved by Chandigarh has an average punishment timeline of just 140 days. It means completing the entire judicial process in less than six months and putting the accused behind bars," he said..Shah appealed to Chandigarh Police to make the fight against drug abuse its priority.."We can move towards a Viksit Bharat only by freeing the younger generation from the menace of drugs," he said..The Union home minister said that the Centre would give AI-enabled 2,152 CCTV cameras to Chandigarh. "With this, Chandigarh will become even safer, and we will be able to firmly ensure the safety of the citizens.".Shah said policing in the country has largely remained focused on tackling terrorism, drugs, cybercrime and maintaining law and order..However, facilitating ease of access to services for citizens is also an important responsibility of the police, he added..He said Chandigarh Police has ensured that whether a citizen needs to obtain a passport, secure a police clearance certificate or a no-objection certificate for employment, or avail of any other service, there is no need for them to visit a police station..He said Chandigarh, which is a Union Territory, has one of the highest vehicle densities in the country.."Before and after becoming the Union home minister, I have visited Chandigarh several times, with and without official protocol, but I have never witnessed a traffic jam here," he said..The response time of the Quick Response Team (QRT) here is 10 minutes, while the police response time is just four minutes, he said..Over 25 schools in Chandigarh receive bomb threat emails; students, staff evacuated .Paying homage to all the martyrs of Chandigarh Police, Shah said laying down one's life in the line of duty -- making the ultimate sacrifice -- is a matter of immense pride for a soldier and also for the organisation to which they belong, he said..He said 141 new vehicles are being inducted into the Chandigarh Police fleet on Sunday. This will significantly strengthen rapid response, intensive patrolling, mobility, technology and modern policing..He said that Chandigarh Police currently ranks second in the country in terms of response time and, with the addition of 141 new vehicles, it will rank first nationwide.

headline: Why do people cyberbully? Bengaluru doctors explain psychology behind online abuse and its after-effects
content: Richa Chaddha famously once said, "Chintu Chandigarh mein baith ke kya soch raha hai, tumhe kya farak padega?"Her remark, which went on to earn an iconic status, came while she was addressing the cyberbullying that Aishwarya Rai Bachchan has faced over her weight during an interaction with Jist Townhall in 2023..However, in reality, if more people, who share similar thoughts with Chintu, join the bandwagon and take to cyberbullying, the outcomes can be far more fatal than what one can fathom.A case in point is the recent death of a 27-year-old Chennai based finance-influencer, who died by suicide on October 20 over an incident of alleged cyberbullying..Kerala woman ends life over cyber-bullying by ex-boyfriend.Earlier in 2025, another young YouTube star Mikayla Raines died at 29 by suicide. The US-based influencer allegedly committed suicide after a malicious campaign of coordinated online rumors and false accusations affected her mental health by and large.There are several such instances where young people have succumbed to cyberbullying.But the pertinent question here is why does one take to cyberbullying? What pleasure do they get out of it?.Why people cyber bully?Dr Sachin Baliga, Consultant - Psychiatrist, Fortis Hospital, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru, says there's no single reason for it."Some will do it out of insecurity, jealousy or anger. Others may use online abuse to feel powerful, get attention or to gain approval from a group. They may have also learned such behaviour from their surroundings," Dr Baliga says.It is important, however, to remember that not all people who bully have been traumatised or have a mental health problem. "Another reason for cyberbullying can be poor emotional control, lack of empathy and inability to understand the impact of one’s actions," Dr Baliga explains. .Chennai-based finance influencer dies by suicide amid cyberbullying, extortion allegations.Woman CPI(M) leader alleges cyberbullying over viral water bottle video.Cyberbullying affecting youth, need to fight it with legislations: Lok Sabha Speaker Birla.While there's no definitive answer as to why do people take to cyberbullying, another commonly perceived notion is the fact hiding behind a screen give bullies a seemingly safe space to not confront the victim."People may feel more comfortable being abusive online because they don’t have to see the other person's reaction. When they talk face-to-face, they know when someone is hurt. That direct connection often is missing online, making it easier to dismiss the sting of their words," Dr Baliga adds.Anonymity can also enable people to feel that they cannot be identified or held responsible. "This could make them less afraid of the consequences. This behaviour can be further encouraged on social media as people see others posting similar comments," he adds.Do cyberbullies realise the damage they cause?Dr Baliga says some people who cyber bully know their words can hurt others but do it anyway because they want attention, control or approval from others. "Others may not realise the impact of their actions (especially if they see their comments as jokes or don’t believe that one comment can do serious harm). Some may even hide behind anonymous accounts to avoid responsibility or fear of judgement. But anonymity doesn't mean a person doesn't know of the harm they are doing. Sometimes people know they are hurting someone, but they think they won't get caught," Dr Baliga shares..Counselling or therapy can help people understand the reasons behind their behaviour, manage their emotions and develop empathy for others. It can also help them learn healthier ways to deal with anger, insecurity and conflict. With the right support and a willingness to change, people can learn to behave more responsibly online.Dr Sachin Baliga, Consultant - Psychiatrist, Fortis Hospital, Bannerghatta Road, Bengaluru.Group behaviour is to be blamedThe most common reason is that they want to be part of a group or get attention through likes, shares and comments. "They may start to think the behaviour is okay when they see other people making fun of someone. This is an example of group behaviour, where people may go along with others without thinking about what effect their actions have," Dr Baliga opines..Online harassment should never be dismissed as merely a virtual problem, because its psychological consequences can be very real.Dr Vinodh Sreeram, Senior Consultant – Adult Psychiatrist & Addiction Specialist, Maarga Mind Care, Bengaluru.The silent struggles of the victimDr Vinodh Sreeram, Senior Consultant – Adult Psychiatrist & Addiction Specialist, Maarga Mind Care, Bengaluru, lists some serious psychological consequences of relentless online harassment:1. Erosion of self-esteem: When someone is repeatedly humiliated in public, it can gradually damage their self worth, dignity and confidence.2. Living in constant fear: Online threats and attacks can leave a person feeling unsafe even in their own home. They may become anxious, hypervigilant and constantly worried about the next attack.3. Social isolation: The fear of being judged and humiliated further may cause the person to withdraw from friends, family and society especially when they need support the most.4. Depression and hopelessness: When the humiliation seems endless, the individual may begin to feel trapped, helpless and unable to see a way out.5. Trauma and PTSD: Severe or threatening experiences can lead to trauma related symptoms, such as intrusive memories, nightmares, disturbed sleep and persistent alertness. "Sometimes, the person who appears silent on the outside may be struggling intensely on the inside. We must recognise the warning signs, respond with empathy rather than judgment, and ensure that the person receives timely professional help," Dr Sreeram explains.Fear of judgement often prevents victims from seeking helpWhat is even more worrisome is the fact that many victims choose to suffer in silence due to fear of judgement, which in the longer run and in many cases, can have fatal outcomes."Many victims remain silent because they fear being judged, blamed or misunderstood. They might be afraid that their family will judge them for what they are doing or that others will make fun of them even more. Some people may be embarrassed, thinking that speaking up will only call more attention to the problem. That fear can add to their emotional distress. People feel lonely and helpless without a safe place to talk about what they are facing," Dr Baliga explains.He concludes, "Families and friends should listen and not blame the victim. They should make the person feel safe and encourage them to seek professional help, if necessary."Counselling or therapy can help people understand the reasons behind their behaviour, manage their emotions and develop empathy for others. It can also help them learn healthier ways to deal with anger, insecurity and conflict. With the right support and a willingness to change, people can learn to behave more responsibly online.Dr Sachin Baliga, Consultant - Psychiatrist, Fortis Hospital, Bannerghatta Road, BengaluruOnline harassment should never be dismissed as merely a virtual problem, because its psychological consequences can be very real.Dr Vinodh Sreeram, Senior Consultant – Adult Psychiatrist & Addiction Specialist, Maarga Mind Care, Bengaluru

headline: Amit Shah mocks Rahul Gandhi's PM ambitions, says he should stay in 'mock Parliament' for life
content: Chandigarh: In a blistering attack on Rahul Gandhi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the country will never forget that the Congress leader held a 'jalsa' on the anniversary of the "Sikh genocide" of 1984, and that if he wanted to become the prime minister, he should stay in a "mock parliament" his entire life..Speaking at an event in Chandigarh, he also slammed opposition parties, saying that telling lies, spreading anarchy and negativity, and not letting Parliament function was their true nature..He was addressing a gathering here after the inauguration and foundation stone-laying ceremony of various development projects worth Rs 258 crore..The opposition I.N.D.I.A. bloc on Sunday held the 'Chalo Dilli' protest at Ramlila Maidan in the national capital as part of its campaign against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities..'Will not escape law': Rahul Gandhi warns PM Modi, Amit Shah of legal action over 'vote chori'.On Saturday, the opposition alliance carried out a symbolic "public impeachment" of CEC Kumar, accusing him of deleting votes to steal elections and demanding that he be tried in court for treason and jailed. The meeting was held in a setting resembling Parliament proceedings at the lawns of Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge. The BJP has described it as a "mockery" of Parliament..Referring to the INDIA bloc rally, Union minister Shah on Sunday said, "If you desire to hold a 'jalsa' for the Congress party on such a dark day of genocide, then Rahul ji, no one will be able to take away anything except hatred from your 'mohabbat ki dukaan'.".Shah said the Congress has been losing elections for 15 years, and its leader Sonia Gandhi's dream of her son becoming the prime minister remains unfulfilled.."So, they have found a new way: conducting a mock parliament. I want to tell Rahul ji, if you want to become the prime minister, stay in the mock parliament your entire life. Your turn (as PM of India) is never going to come," he said..He lashed out at the INDIA bloc leaders for not listening to Delhi traders' request to defer their rally until after Diwali.."The traders of Delhi pleaded with them, saying, 'We have just one day, one week in the entire year when our business thrives. If we stock up on sweets and they don't sell, what will happen? It will lead to losses. If we buy firecrackers and they don't sell, what will happen? It will lead to losses'," said Shah.."A trade worth Rs 25,000 crore takes place in these 3-4 days. The whole of north India comes to Delhi's wholesale market to buy Diwali goods," he said.."But no, on the very day the Sikh riots happened, the Sikh genocide happened, on that very day, on that same dark day, they had to hold a rally," he said..Rahul Gandhi's rally in Delhi will only rub salt in wounds of anti-Sikh riot victims: Amit Shah."Now remember my words: for the next three elections, your account is not going to open there," he added..On the anti-Sikh riots, he said, "On November 1, 1984, thousands of Sikhs were brutally murdered in Delhi during riots incited by the Congress party.."Thousands of Sikhs were burnt alive. Many Sikhs had to leave their homes, many children were orphaned, many sisters were widowed, and homes of many were burnt," Shah said..He recalled remarks by former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi that "when a big tree falls, the earth shakes."."I saw that statement on television, and I can never forget it in my lifetime," Shah said of Rajiv Gandhi's remarks in the aftermath of Indira Gandhi's assassination in 1984..To describe the brutal killing of thousands of Sikhs in such a way is something that only Congress leaders could do, he said.."Today, his son Rahul Gandhi organised a 'bada jalsa' in Delhi to rub salt into the wounds of the victims of the 1984 riots and their families.".The BJP held a press conference and had asked the I.N.D.I.A. bloc not to hold its rally on November 1, 2 and 3, as on these days, the anti-Sikh riots took place, Shah said.."This deeply hurt our Sikh brothers, mothers, sisters, and children. Yet they insisted. From abroad, an order was issued to their party for holding the 'jalsa' on the very same day when thousands of Sikhs were set ablaze," he said..Shah said he strongly condemns and criticises their "malicious attempt". "India and Punjab will never forget this.".Shah said when the Modi government came to power, it reopened all the cases related to the anti-Sikh riots.."We provided financial assistance of Rs 5 lakh each to the riot victims and ensured that prominent Congress leaders involved in the riots were sent behind bars," he said..India had never witnessed politically instigated riots of this nature before, and I hope it never has to witness such riots again, he asserted..Shah said the Narendra Modi government is taking the country forward by leaps and bounds.."Article 370 was abolished, Naxalism was ended, Triple Talaq was abolished," he said. "Now remember my words: on December 31, 2029, we will make the entire country, including Punjab, drug-free," he asserted.."The largest cricket stadium, the highest overbridge, the longest bridge, all of these are being built in India, worth Rs 11 lakh crore. Electricity has reached every poor person's home," the minister added..Shah alleged that Rahul Gandhi does not let Parliament run because he does not want women to get 33 per cent reservation.."Rahul Baba, I want to tell you that this very Narendra Modi ji will give 33 per cent reservation to 'nari shakti' of India. This is our resolve," said Shah..The people of the country are watching all these things very closely, he said..Amit Shah kicks off Uttar Pradesh BJP meet; party sets 325-350 seat target for 2027 polls."Who is making the country safe? Who is making the country developed? Who brought innovation to the country? Who brought the new education policy? Who is making the country economically prosperous?.The public of the country is seeing all these things, and all of this will be accounted for in the 2029 elections. Rahul ji, remember my words," said the Union minister..Shah said that in the coming days, the central government will make Chandigarh the number one administrative unit of the country..He also exuded confidence that an NDA government will be formed in the border state after the next assembly elections.

headline: Chandigarh Budget (2026-2027) : A Department-wise Review
source: IMPRI Impact and Policy Research Institute
content: Chandigarh’s scheme architecture combines locally administered welfare programmes, centrally sponsored schemes and public infrastructure projects financed through the Union Budget. Chandigarh is a Union Territory without a legislature, therefore, its expenditure is presented under the Ministry of Home Affairs’ Demand No. 53. Consequently, its departmental priorities must be read through Union budget documents, Chandigarh Administration’s departmental records and the programmes implemented by its public institutions. For 2026–27, Chandigarh’s gross budget provision is Rs 6,545.52 crore, comprising Rs 5,939.52 crore in revenue expenditure and Rs 606 crore in capital expenditure. This compares with a gross budget estimate of Rs 6,983.18 crore in 2025–26 and a revised estimate of Rs 6,465.77 crore (Ministry of Finance, Government of India, 2026). The 2026–27 provision is therefore lower than the preceding year’s original allocation but slightly above its revised estimate. After recoveries, the net provision is Rs 5,720.17 crore. The principal policy question is how Chandigarh will sustain welfare and service delivery while financing infrastructure within this budget envelope. Education, health facilities, public transport, renewable energy, social protection and urban services feature prominently in the expenditure framework. However, the budget’s “Schemes of UT” allocations do not represent complete departmental budgets; salaries, institutional grants and other expenditures appear under separate heads. Latest Budget Provision: Rs 87.06 Cr in gross capital expenditure in the 2026–27 budget under “Urban Development” and Rs 36.05 Cr under “Government Housing” Scheme 1: Urban Infrastructure and Civic Works, Key Details: Land acquisition and surveys, infrastructure development, urban roads, stormwater drainage, electrification, civic works and infrastructure serving the Information Technology Park, Coverage: Urban infrastructure across Chandigarh. Individual project allocations are not separately identified in the summary document. Scheme 2: Government Building Construction and Renovation, Key Details: Construction and renovation of residential and non-residential government buildings, Coverage: Government accommodation and public-service buildings. This should not be described as an allocation for affordable housing for the general public.

headline: Rahul Gandhi's rally in Delhi will only rub salt in wounds of anti-Sikh riot victims: Amit Shah
content: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Sunday launched an attack on Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over the I.N.D.I.A. bloc’s rally in Delhi on the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, saying the event would only “rub salt in the wounds” of the victims.Addressing a gathering in Chandigarh after inaugurating and laying the foundation stones for development projects worth Rs 258 crore, Shah questioned the Congress’ decision to organise the rally on November 1, the day the anti-Sikh violence broke out in 1984 following the assassination of then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi..Sea of flags at Ramlila Maidan: I.N.D.I.A. bloc's rally goes beyond 'vote chori'. “Rahul Gandhi’s November 1 ‘jalsa’ in Delhi will only rub salt in wounds of anti-Sikh riot victims,” Shah said. “The day the Sikh genocide happened, on that very day, they had to hold a rally,” he added, referring to the I.N.D.I.A. bloc’s ‘Chalo Dilli’ rally at Ramlila Maidan against alleged electoral irregularities and demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Recalling former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s controversial remark following the 1984 riots -- “When a big tree falls, the earth shakes” -- Shah said that thousands of Sikhs were killed in the violence, while several families were forced to leave their homes, children were orphaned and women widowed..Foolish drama, will be final nail in coffin of Congress' political future: JP Nadda on Sunday rally. “Thousands of Sikhs were burnt alive. Many Sikhs had to leave their homes, many children were orphaned, many sisters were widowed and homes of many were burnt,” he said.The Home Minister alleged that the Congress had ignored repeated appeals from the BJP to avoid holding its rally on November 1, 2 and 3, given the significance of these dates for the Sikh community.“We thought he might have been too young at the time and, since he does not read history, perhaps he would not know about it,” Shah said, referring to Rahul Gandhi.He further alleged that the Congress had received instructions from abroad to hold the rally on the very day thousands of Sikhs were killed.Shah also accused the Congress of spreading lies, creating anarchy and disrupting parliamentary proceedings. “If you want to become Prime Minister, stay in a ‘mock Parliament’ your entire life. Your turn will never come,” he said.
